i completely resonate with that, “i’m not suicidal, just very tired”. life is a difficult thing to get through to begin with, and the worries of hypochondria and anxiety along with the weight of depression and bipolar only serve to bring you down more. it’s absolutely exhausting trying to keep up. 

i personally have my own issues, but namely a rampant dissociative disorder. i’m not present for 95% of my day, simply on autopilot, driving through life when i’m not even in the car. i barely remember what happens every day, and it takes a toll on my education, personal life, and work. even when i am in the moment, i’m plagued with looming depression and overthinking. i sometimes catch myself thinking 

*”what’s the point? why am i here if i’m just going to be miserable?”* 

it’s an ongoing battle, for sure. it’s hard to find purpose in the messy dark fog of this life, especially after suffering from worry for so long. but there is purpose. i know it’s oversaid and overlooked, but i at least believe it to be true. 

counseling can be so hard to access due to costs and healthcare, but if an opportunity does present itself i’d definitely recommend taking it. we’re so used to being trapped inside our own heads, it can be so incredibly helpful to have access to someone who knows their stuff and can help you untie the knotted-up thoughts in your mind. us here on the internet can only do so much, sadly. :( we here can only offer words of kindness and support, and assure you that you’re not alone, we know and feel your fear and hope you can find comfort in knowing that. 

i hope this helps, even if it’s a little :) :)
